newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow sees Ukraine sugar output under 3 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow sees Ukraine sugar output under 3 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine's sugar production could fall below official predictions of more than 3.0 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, although the final figure will depend on the severity and timing of winter, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.

In its latest report, Czarnikow said its initial August forecast of 2.55 million tonnes was probably too pessimistic, although there would undoubtedly be a fall from last season's 3.79 million tonnes.
But Czarnikow cast doubt on official forecasts for the 1996/97 crop of more than 3.0 million tonnes of sugar from a harvest of 26 million tonnes of beet.
"This may be optimistic and the final figure may drop below this, depending on the severity and timing of winter," it said.
Ukrainian farmers were not in a position to delay their late harvest as the onset of winter weather would put an end to practical field work.
Czarnikow said the Ukrainian harvest had been beset by equipment and fuel shortages as well as freuqent breakdowns.
